title: Assembling fiber colimit cones on a Grothendieck collage
statement: Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimits as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $I$ be a small ordinary category and $U:I\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a strict functor to small ordinary categories. Define $K=\int_I U$: its objects are $(i,x)$ with $x\in U(i)$, and a morphism $(i,x)\to(j,y)$ is $(f,\alpha)$ with $f:i\to j$ and $\alpha:U(f)(x)\to y$, composed by $(g,\beta)(f,\alpha)=(gf,\beta\,U(g)(\alpha))$. Write $p:K\to I$ for projection. Define the collage $P$ with disjoint full subcategories $K$ and $I$, with $\operatorname{Hom}_P(k,i)=\operatorname{Hom}_I(p(k),i)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_P(i,k)=\varnothing$; mixed composition uses $p$ and composition in $I$. Let $Q:N(K)\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent diagram in a quasicategory. Suppose $Q_i=Q|_{N(U(i))}$ has a colimit for every $i\in I$. Then there exists $\overline Q:N(P)\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $Q$, such that the cocone on $Q_i$ with apex $\overline Q(i)$ induced by the arrows $(i,x)\to i$ labeled $1_i$ is colimiting, for every $i$. Empty fibers require initial objects. No preservation of colimits by $U(f)$ or by $Q$ is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 7.3.4.7 (02ZW), with target base the point, together with Proposition 7.3.4.3 (02ZP). Apply to the nerve of the Grothendieck projection; its chosen cocartesian lifts are (f,identity), and its relative join with N(I) is the nerve of the displayed collage. Both pages read online; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.
